Friday 18 December 2026 · Year A · Identity & Belonging · 40 minutes

The scheme objective is to add evidence to the independence portfolio. Assess selection, explanation and storage through actual earlier work. A portfolio label or retrospective account alone does not establish an earlier practical skill. No new practical skill is taught or tested in this lesson.

Before teaching, gather each learner’s available work and dated observations from Weeks 1–6. Check ownership, original dates and storage references. Start the six-week audit without pre-judging the learner’s review. Provide the usual aid, folder, evidence sheet and support cards. Keep peer records private. Plan short individual review turns during slides 6–8; learners waiting can look through their own work. If there is no earlier work, prepare a gap record rather than a model answer or replacement practical task.

Read the same prompts without suggesting an explanation. Record the learner’s own words, pointing or aid response before feedback. Reading and exact scribing are access help. A supplied claim, model, corrected explanation or reduced choice is content support. Record the type and timing. Separate help on the earlier task from help with today’s review and filing.
An available piece or dated observation belongs to the learner and links to a taught week. Record its code, original date and location. A supported choice remains valid when the help is clear.
The learner identifies an action or contribution and points to a relevant clue. Their account agrees with the earlier record, including adult help. Record uncertainty instead of filling a gap.
The actual work is filed or a usable reference points to its storage location. Preserve the original date. Existing filed work can be cross-referenced without counting it as a new achievement.
After feedback, the learner gives or chooses a response and one familiar skill or gap to revisit. Record needed help and a review date. Keep this later response separate.

Answers depend on actual work. Do not supply fictional completed evidence. A blank sheet, adult model, peer product or checklist tick without a work reference is insufficient. A shared product requires a dated record of the learner’s own contribution.

Audit all six weeks using earlier work and observations. Use available, partial, missing or not observed. Record original dates and support. The audit is an index, not proof of every skill.

Retain the gap and record what is missing. Seek an existing dated observation or work reference. If none exists, arrange a separate familiar-skill check later and date it honestly. Today’s help request or portfolio discussion is evidence only of what occurred today; it does not replace a missing recipe, cleaning or making observation.
